title: Mr. PinPin and the Timber Tractor: Complete Production Journal
lead: A standalone woodland adventure, from clean camera plates to a twenty-scene family edition awaiting user review.
statusLabel: Twenty reading images per language; 22 unique selected assets across three languages. All 29 earlier outputs are retained alongside four family outputs: 33 successful outputs and three failed requests. The family art is unapproved and awaiting user review.
scope: Original standalone fiction inspired by the friendly farm story, using the main-book camera-first workflow.
eyebrow: Mr. PinPin / Standalone adventures / Camera notebook
sourceNotes: This is new fiction, not a chapter of the original book. The farm story informs the warm friendship and vehicle-discovery rhythm. The beaver replaces the farm bear as the driver for this standalone adventure.

The approved title image fixes the red tractor, yellow crane and main-book PinPin design. Clean locations branch from that visual anchor. The missing bridge boards, windfallen wood and willow-twig joke are story inventions approved in outline.

Original Mama illustration image55 supplies mother-child proportions and family warmth. Scene-19 adapts that reference to the modern brown-quill and cream-fur rendering; it does not establish a fixed canonical Mama design. Later family scenes use that adapted identity.

Scene-19 (family arrival) and scene-20 (supervised steering with the tractor parked, not actual driving) are inserted after scene-14 and before the picnic. Scene-15-v2 and scene-18-v2 replace the two earlier picnic images. Six superseded candidates remain in the journal: scene-06, scene-07, scene-09, scene-11, scene-15 and scene-18. Five additional successful outputs are intermediate environment plates.
steps: Extend the original eighteen-scene story to twenty scenes in English, Spanish and Russian with two family insertions before the picnic.
Generate clean environments using camera position, direction and scene state.
Establish the beaver and PinPin together, then add each scene's full cast directly without colored-limb blocking.
Inspect scale, faces, limb attachments, eyelines, crane/load state and bridge continuity.
Compose vertical reading and explicit print pages, separating joke setup from reveal.
Verify local and published reader, multilingual text and PDF; preserve prompts and all attempts.
conclusion: Twenty reading images per language use 22 unique assets including localized covers. The four family candidates remain unapproved pending user review; an automated audit is not visual approval. All 33 successful outputs and three failed requests remain documented, including the failed first scene-18-v2 request. Final PDF and live-reader checks are documented separately before release.

shots.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: a 1536×1024 landscape children's book illustration, scene20 of Mr. PinPin and the Timber Tractor.
Input images: Image1 is the exact EDIT TARGET, showing the parked tractor, PinPin at the controls, supervising Beaver, and Mama plus baby PomPom outside. Image2 is a tractor geometry reference only. Image3 is a tractor model/reference for correct hood, cab, and wheel relationships only; do NOT import its load or travelling scene.
Primary request: Correct the physically backwards steering layout in Image1. The red engine hood and tractor nose point toward IMAGE LEFT, and the rear tractor wheel, trailer, and crane are toward IMAGE RIGHT. Therefore the operator seat, PinPin's torso and legs, and the steering column must all face LEFT toward the engine hood. The SINGLE steering wheel must be AHEAD OF PinPin on his LEFT toward the hood, not on his right toward the back of the cab. Remove the existing wrong rear/right-side wheel and dashboard/column. Put the dashboard and steering-column base at the actual FRONT of the cab, directly behind the engine hood/front windshield on the LEFT. A clearly connected column rises from this forward dashboard/floor and tilts back toward PinPin's paws. One operator seat with its cushion pointing left and its backrest behind PinPin toward the RIGHT/rear. PinPin sits on this main operator seat and reaches both paws FORWARD/LEFT to the one steering wheel. The seat, body, steering wheel, column, front windshield, and engine hood must form one readable aligned forward-driving direction.
Camera and readability: You may adjust the camera to an exterior front three-quarter view through the open near-side door so PinPin's recognizable face remains visible in profile or with a small head turn toward the viewer, while his body and seat still face the engine front. Do not simply mirror the whole image. Keep the tractor's nose toward image LEFT and trailer toward image RIGHT. Preserve the warm original composition as much as possible while making the correct geometry obvious.
Characters and story invariants: The tractor is parked with engine off, no movement, no exhaust smoke. This is an imaginary driving game, not actual driving. Beaver in his blue work vest supervises warmly from behind/beside PinPin and is not occupying an opposing driver's position. Mama and much smaller baby PomPom remain outside on the ground at foreground RIGHT, watching happily, with their original distinct identities and relative sizes. Keep all FOUR characters; no new character and no duplicate PinPin. Keep PinPin's expressive established hedgehog face and warm tan/cream fur and quills. Preserve the family, completed wooden bridge, stream, bright woodland, daisies, and sunny storybook rendering.
Machinery invariants: Red engine hood and smaller tractor front wheel at LEFT; cab above the larger rear wheel; empty two-axle timber trailer attached BEHIND the cab to RIGHT with dark frame and red-tipped stakes. Yellow crane remains mounted on the trailer-front frame immediately behind the cab, not at the far rear. No load of logs. Only ONE steering wheel, one coherent steering column, and one operator seat. The compact passenger seat may be folded out of view; do not add an extra opposing chair. Do not attach steering to the rear window, door pillar, or side door.
Avoid: backwards operator seating, steering at the rear, duplicated wheels/controls/chairs, mirrored whole scene, missing family, swapped baby/adult sizes, text, captions, watermarks, or changing this into a moving tractor scene.

carryForwardNotes: Clean landscape plates and concise camera direction establish each location before characters enter. Each scene's visible cast is added together from a shared identity reference, without colored-limb blocking.

Small faces inside a distant cab need enlarged review, not just a whole-image glance. The user identified PinPin's travel face as malformed; a targeted repair was reviewed and selected without redesigning the rest of that image.

Independent review caught softened beaver identity in cab views and squared timber appearing too early. Corrected versions are kept alongside the original candidates; the reader selects only the reviewed final paths.

A believable image is not proof of exact anatomy, machinery, load restraint or camera geometry. Hidden limbs stay unverified. Minor grille, hub and botanical variation is documented rather than described as perfect continuity.

The family review checks all four actual PNGs for Mama/baby identity, faces and duplicated forelimb attachments. No confirmed duplicate attachments were found, but concealed joints remain unverified. Baby size and apparent age vary; the picnic baby is larger relative to PinPin than the requested half-height. The finale broadly preserves the family picnic identity. Family approval remains with the user.
